geophys.title: Historic England · Методы археологической геофизики
geophys.passage: Magnetic variations can reveal burned iron minerals and filled ditches. Resistance instruments inject a small current through ground electrodes; moist fills and masonry often yield different responses. GPR records return time and amplitude of reflected radiofrequency pulses and can survey paved surfaces.

lidar.title: Historic England · Воздушное лазерное сканирование
lidar.passage: Pulsed airborne laser builds a terrain model and can reveal shallow features and remains under woodland.

cannock.title: Historic England · Воздушная съёмка Каннок-Чейса
cannock.passage: Filtering vegetation revealed ground outlines of First World War camp huts and trenches.

aerial.title: Historic England · Аэрофотоснимки в археологии
aerial.passage: Archived aerial photographs from different years include vertical and oblique records of archaeological sites and buildings.

photo.title: Historic England · Фотограмметрия и другие методы съёмки
photo.passage: Photogrammetry uses images to measure and record heritage objects and features, including 3D reconstruction from overlapping photos.

sat.title: Historic England · Спутниковая и многоспектральная съёмка
sat.passage: Discusses optical and other satellite imagery, and monitoring damage and changes to heritage sites.

cores.title: Музей каменных орудий · Нуклеусы и отщепы
cores.passage: Types of cores include bifacial, single-platform and multiplatform examples; strikes along platforms remove flakes.

workshop.title: Музей каменных орудий · Нуклеусы, отщепы и следы сколов
workshop.passage: Workshop covers negative flake scars, ventral and dorsal surfaces, impact point, platform and percussion bulb. A flake from Queensland has an intact weathered cortex on the striking platform.

blades.title: Музей каменных орудий · Пластины и пластинчатые нуклеусы
blades.passage: A blade is at least twice as long as wide. Blade production uses long ridges and can produce nearly parallel sides; some Australian macroblades were mounted as knives and traded.

waste.title: Колледж Вильгельма и Марии · Археологический глоссарий
waste.passage: Debitage consists of debris from knapping stone; flakes are produced during manufacture.

analysis.title: Висконсинский университет в Ла-Кроссе · Анализ каменных находок
analysis.passage: Shows core, waste flakes, hammerstone, bifaces, points, end scraper, drill and utilized flake as distinct archaeological material. Sorting lithic objects helps interpret activity and technology.

mid.title: Смитсоновский институт · Орудия среднего каменного века
mid.passage: Stone scrapers prepared hide, wood and other materials. Stone awls were used to perforate hides. Hafted points formed spears.

hammer.title: Смитсоновский институт · Каменные орудия ранних людей
hammer.passage: Hammerstones could be used for cracking nuts and struck cobbles to make cutting flakes.

adze.title: Музей каменных орудий · Каменное тесло Новой Гвинеи
adze.passage: Documented Langda adzes are elongated and triangular in cross-section; their cutting edge was ground and unground scars sometimes colored with ochre.

retouch.title: Музей каменных орудий · Ретушированные отщепы
retouch.passage: Retouching uses percussion and sometimes pressure; fan scrapers could be retouched along one face, and tula adzes were sometimes exchanged.

earlyTools.title: Смитсоновский институт · Ранние каменные орудия
earlyTools.passage: Hammerstones show battering on their surfaces.

emi.title: Агентство по охране окружающей среды США · Электромагнитная съёмка
emi.passage: Frequency-domain electromagnetic methods use transmitting and receiving coils to sense conductivity changes in the subsurface; listed applications include archaeological surveys.

note: CURRENT revises reciprocal method and lithic clue transfers. The archaeological LiDAR prompt is based on canopy filtering and leaves the laser travel-time discriminator to maps-cartography.
